messages:
Ada Chen: Quick decision needed — FinCorp pilot just asked for 95p <120ms on chat generation. They’re willing to commit reserved spend if we can guarantee it for launch in ~6 weeks. Options: 1) Dedicated hotpath: route FinCorp traffic to reserved nodes + KV prefetch + perf kernels — fastest but highest ongoing cost. 2) Workload-optimized serving (per-model kernel tweaks, targeted quant) + prefix cache — medium latency, medium effort. 3) SLO compromise + credits/discounts — low engineering cost, higher product risk.
Ada Chen: I want a pragmatic prioritization using RICE but adding a simple "regret" multiplier (how bad is it if we say no). Link to short spec: https://redwood.internal/s/fin-sla (one-pager) — please read the TL;DR and vote with reactions :one:/:two:/:three:.
Matt Liu: From runtime POV, option 1 is straightforward ops work: add customer routing + dedicate a small pool. ~2 sprints (eng-runtime + infra) to be comfortable. Latency win will be clear. Cost estimate: ~30-40% increase on that customer's bill relative to shared serving.
Sasha Patel: Dedicated pool needs isolation (netpols + KMS scoping) and SLO config in console. We can provision in our EU region but need quota requests for GPUs; that lead time could be 2-3 weeks. Also: autoscale behavior for reserved pools needs a hard cap to avoid surprises.
Noah Rivera: From product/GT I care about speed to revenue. FinCorp is high-impact (pilot => enterprise contract). RICE-ish quick calc: Reach=8 (pilot large), Impact=9 (revenue + logo), Confidence=6 (we haven't run their traffic shape), Effort: option1=4 (lower = more effort), option2=6, option3=9. If we do R*I*C/E (tiny heuristic): opt1 ~ (8*9*6)/4=108, opt2~(8*7*6)/6=56, opt3~(8*3*7)/9=18. Plus regret multiplier: opt1 x1.0, opt2 x1.2 (because long term ops risk), opt3 x1.6 (high regret). That still favors opt1.
Priya Kapoor: Important: option1 increases unit cost but preserves quality. If sales can convert pilot to committed reserved spend, we likely recoup. Also consider a hybrid: start with opt1 for initial weeks, simultaneously land opt2 improvements to reduce cost mid-term. That spreads risk.
Matt Liu: Hybrid is workable. Implementation sketch: week1-2: provision reserved pool + traffic route. week2-6: ship kernel/quant improvements and prefix caching. Roll traffic progressively. Need a canary plan and fallback to shared model.
Sasha Patel: +1 on canary. Also add traces and a short eval harness: run FinCorp test prompts through both paths and compare 95/99p latencies before cutting over.
Noah Rivera: Can we get a quick deployment config example?
Matt Liu: Here’s a tiny routing snippet we can add to service config:```json
{"routes": [{"matcher": "customer_id==\"fincorp\"", "pool": "reserved-fincorp-eu", "fallback": "shared"}]}
```
Matt Liu: And an SLO rule: 95p latency <120ms, alert if 95p >130ms for 5m.
Priya Kapoor: Sales feedback: FinCorp will accept a 2-week trial with committed $ value if we can show <120ms 95p in a pre-cutover run. They want a written acceptance criteria doc. I can draft.
Ada Chen: Quick risks: capacity lead time (Sasha), engineering bandwidth (Matt), and cost negotiation (Priya). Proposal: approve hybrid approach (opt1 immediate + opt2 medium-term). Action items: Sasha request quotas + provision reserved pool; Matt implement routing + canary; Eng-ML build perf eval harness + kernel experiments; Noah/Priya finalize acceptance doc. Can we commit to timelines?
Sasha Patel: I’ll open the quota request today and provision a placeholder pool. ETA: pool provisioned in 10 business days if quotas approved.
Matt Liu: I’ll spike routing + canary this sprint. If Sasha gets pool earlier I’ll cut traffic canary within 48h.
Noah Rivera: I’ll coordinate acceptance doc and the customer test run. Draft ready by Friday.
Ada Chen: OK — consensus reached via :one:/:two: reaction mix (mostly :one: and :two:). Final decision: greenlight hybrid (dedicated hotpath now, parallel optimization work). I’ll file PRD update and timeline.
deploy-bot: New task created: #task-2158 "FinCorp SLA: provision reserved pool + routing" assigned to Sasha Patel, Matt Liu, Eng-ML. Due 2026-04-15.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks all — I’ll sync with FinCorp and schedule the trial run next week. :thumbsup:
